title.narrative: Stöd till polisreform basket via UNODC
Support police reform basket via UNODC

description.narrative: Stöd till basket fund för polisreform administrerad av UNODC för perioden 2013-2015.
Support to basket fund for police reform administered by UNODC during the period 2013-2015.

The programme has been hampered by the lack of will by the political leadership for reforms as per the 2010 Constitution of Kenya. The police has traditionally been used to keep opposition and unwanted forces (not only of criminal nature) at bay, not least during election years. The lack of support from the Kenyan leadership is also one of the main reasons for the Embassy decision to end its support after many years of support in various forms, once this programme ended. As concluded in the evaluation, which covered the whole project period 2013-2017, the design of the project lacked clear frameworks for results and monitoring, and the concluding report (as previous reports) consequently lacks clear results, but focuses more on outputs. The attempt by the cooperation partner to analyse the achieved, partly achieved or not achieved targets under each indicator lacks depth and is more of recommendations for a 'way forward' - addressee unknown, since there is no continuation of the project components. The PO has followed up with discussions with individual staff at UNODC who have not been able to bring more clarity to the programme. However, in confidence, staff members have confirmed the conclusion made above, that there has not been real political will 'at the top' to reform the force. One of the most important reforms was for the two police forces inherited from colonial times; the Kenya Police and the Administration Police have not managed to merge, but have continued to exist relatively independent of the other. In terms of results that have been achieved, it is reasonable to assume some changes have been accomplished in pockets at station level through a few drivers of change within the police. This programme may have contributed to the knowledge and skills for individual commanders and officers but it is not possible to determin the lasting effect as of yet. The support of the police can, however, be viewed as one of the many small steps to slowly change the mindsets of individuals in rigid organisations, which one day will reach a critical mass to tip them over to embark on an effective reform process. The UK continues to fund the reforms and hence, their efforts may be helped by work done by this programme in some of the counties. The Embassy has continued to support the demand for accountability, transparency and service delivery from the police through its programme with Diakonia (phase II 2018-2021), which also includes training of police officers and supporting community dialogue forums, and push for the reforms to go on.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
